results.reason: The abstract describes a search-based technique for unit test generation on object-oriented programs that reaches high coverage, matching the sentence.
The abstract reports that test suites detecting more mutants also detect more real faults, so mutation scores are a useful proxy, matching the sentence.
The abstract finds 14 percent of CI test failures were caused by flaky tests, which supports the claim that flaky tests are common in continuous integration.
The abstract describes a genetic algorithm guiding unit test generation toward a coverage target. The citing sentence attributes only the GA search style to this work, which is consistent with it.
The abstract describes a fuzzer that uses coverage feedback to find crashes, consistent with coverage-guided input mutation as used in fuzzing.
The abstract says the genetic algorithm maximizes branch coverage and does not mention mutants, so the coverage-optimization claim matches. The no-mutants part is not stated but is not contradicted.
The abstract is a study of whether mutants are a valid substitute for real faults, which matches the sentence citing mutation analysis studies as motivation for using mutants.
The abstract measures how common flaky tests are in CI test failures (14 percent), which matches the sentence's description of the work.
The abstract describes a coverage-feedback fuzzer that finds crashes, consistent with the sentence saying fuzzers share input mutation but target crashes.
